items.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So I settled on the trombone because Tommy Dorsey was the big thing.

ctx.x: And did you early on have any music lessons there, or, besides your father taking you and exposing you to these wonderful bands...

Well I wanted to play drums, and I’d still like to play drums, but I don’t have much talent for it. But my mother said no because we lived like in a basement apartment. She was afraid it would break our lease and make noise. So I settled on the trombone because Tommy Dorsey was the big thing. So I took a year of that with a great trombonist from the Jan Savitt band, and took a year, and I couldn’t remember where anything went with the trombone, so that was that. I never could play it. But I had an old King that I…
So what neighborhood did you live in in Philly?
